newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 23.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
LALOO LOYALISTS GO ON OFFENSIVE

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is all set to file a chargesheet against Bihar state Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav. His supporters in New Delhi on Sunday for the first time accused former Prime Minister Deve Gowda of conspiring to destabilise the Bihar government. Deputies and ministers loyal to Yadav warned Prime Minister Gujral against the raid raj (raid regime) allegedly let loose against the chief minister by investigating authorities.
The Economic Times
INDIA REFUSES TO GO WITH U.S. ON BROADCASTING

India has told the United States that economic liberalisation and the broadcast policy cannot be treated on a par. The government said the two issues had to be treated separately and that the broadcasting sector was not just another sector of industry that was being opened up. It pointed out the proposed legislation on broadcasting was not conservative but liberal. These were conveyed to the US government during the recent visit to the United States by Indian officials who included the cabinet secretary.
OIL REFORM PACKAGE BOASTS TWIN-EDGED LINEUP

To tackle the swelling oil pool deficit the government decided to dovetail it into a longer-term perspective on the country's oil policy. It is working out a comprehensive reform package which is expected to nurse the oil economy back to health as well as be acceptable to the political parties. The package will be unveiled soon. Its features include a novel proposal of a 'windfall tax' on oil companies. Otherwise, there will be a marginal oil price hike, steps to dismantle the administered price mechanism and a phased reduction in the tariff on crude imports to levels recommended at a World Trade Organisation meeting.
GUJRAL PUSHES FOR EXPORT GROWTH; MEET ON JUNE 26

Prime Minister Gujral has convened a meeting on June 26 to evolve both short term and medium term strategies to put India back on a high export growth path of over 20 percent. The commerce ministry feels that without this the country will find it difficult to catch up with the Asian tigers. The commerce minister will hold a meeting with a select group of exporters and export organisations on Wednesday to assess the problems.
Business Standard
INFLATION DIPS FURTHER TO 5.83 PER CENT

The annual rate of inflation based on wholesale price index declined by 0.1 percentage point to 5.83 percent for the week ended June 7. The steady decline in inflation is mainly due to a fall in the prices of primary articles over the last three months. The prices of vegetables plunged 20.72 percent since February. The annual inflation (provisional) calculated on a point-to-point basis eased to 5.83 percent in the reference week from 5.93 percent a week earlier. The rate of inflation during the corresponding week last year was 4.52 percent.
The Observer
CREDIT FACILITY LIKELY TO BE RESTORED

Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum are considering reopening of the credit facility to scheduled airlines to buy aviation turbine fuel. Unlike the earlier practice, the dues will now be collected within a specified time which will be decided on a case- to-case basis. Any defaulter will be removed from the list of favourite clientele and prosecuted, said a senior Hindustan Petroleum official. Sources in the oil companies agree that reopening the credit is primarily because of the prevailing competition among the oil companies to gain maximum market share.
BANKS' LENDING DOWN BY 8.28 BLN RUPEES IN THREE MONTHS

The total lendings or advances by scheduled commercial banks in the first quarter of fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) went down by 8.28 billion rupees from 49 billion rupees during the same period last fiscal. While banks' lending activities slowed down, their investments nearly doubled to 104.69 billion rupees in the first quarter of this fiscal, shows a Reserve Bank analysis. The Reserve Bank is yet to compile figures of banks' investments in the corporate securities. It observed that a lot of money was being circulated this year through commercial papers and debentures.
NYLON PRICES DIP DESPITE OUTPUT CUT

Nylon yarn prices have dropped by about eight rupees to 10 rupees a kg in the last three weeks. This is due to an absence of demand from weavers. The weavers say their offtake is reduced basically due to a sluggish demand for the fibre and cloth as well as due to power cuts and labour shortage. Nylon yarn has become cheaper in spite of a cut in production by its major producers. Sources close to the spinners said with the last budget nylon substitutes like polypropylene, viscose and polyester yarns became cheaper.
The Economic Times
DOCUMENT TO REVEAL TRACK RECORD OF LEAD MANAGERS

The stock market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has decided to incorporate a new disclosure norm seeking background of intermediaries in the public issue offer documents. The norm is being introduced to provide investors information about the track record of lead managers to a public or rights issue. The provision will incorporate information on merchant bankers, including penalties levied by SEBI for non-compliance with regulations or defaults, investigations conducted against the intermediaries and suspension or cancellation notices issued against them.
Business Standard
NEW PACKAGE SOON TO BOOST POWER SECTOR INVESTMENTS

The government will soon announce a package of measures to augment the country's power policy framework. The new package is aimed at boosting investment in the sector. It is slated to include an alternative to the financial guarantees by the federal government and measures to attract funds from financial institutions. The package also envisages a greater role for public sector entities like the National Thermal Power Corporation. The federal counter-guarantees may be replaced by World Bank guarantees for those state governments which are prepared to restructure their state electricity boards.
ASHOK JAIN QUITS EXECUTIVE POSTS IN ALL GROUP FIRMS

Media baron Ashok Jain resigned from various posts held in group companies on medical grounds. These include the post of the managing director on Bennett Coleman, the publishers of The Times of India newspaper and many other publications. But he will continue as the chairman of Bennett Coleman.
